rounds.lesson: The audio transcript in the tweet ('4th Tactical Fighter Wing', 'Al-Kharj', 'Scud missiles and chemical facilities') are highly specific Desert Storm identifiers. Searching the pilot name + unit details immediately surfaces the 1991 origin. The claimed event date (April 2026) vs. no corroborating news is itself a strong signal.

rounds.what_returned: axpow.org bio, National Air and Space Museum, valor.militarytimes.com, pownetwork.org all confirm Col. David W. Eberly. Shot down January 19, 1991 over Iraq. Captured on Syrian border after evading 3 nights. Released March 6, 1991. 4th Fighter Wing, F-15E, based at Al-Kharj, Saudi Arabia. Book 'Faith Beyond Belief' (2002).
rounds.lesson: The pilot's real name (Eberly) is close to the audio rendering ('Iberly') — a phonetic near-match. Multiple authoritative military record sources confirm all details. Anti-hindsight check: the audio transcript in the tweet contained enough specifics (unit name, base location, target type) to identify this as Gulf War footage without prior knowledge.

what_helped: The audio transcript in the tweet contained highly specific identifiers (unit name '4th Tactical Fighter Wing', base location 'Al-Kharj', target type 'Scud missiles and chemical facilities') that are unique to Desert Storm and immediately surfaced the 1991 origin
Searching the pilot name from the audio ('Iberly' → real name 'Eberly') directly returned fact-checks and POW records
Searching the claimed event date ('US pilot captured Iraq April 2026') immediately surfaced multiple dedicated fact-checks — no corroborating news existed for a 2026 capture
The combination of specific military unit + base location + target type is a fingerprint unique enough that a single targeted query was sufficient
what_hurt: The audio phonetic rendering 'Iberly' vs. real name 'Eberly' could have been a barrier if searching only the exact audio text — though search engines handled this well

The tweet uses 'Iraq' while some fact-checks frame it as 'Iran' (because some parallel versions of the misinformation claimed capture in Iran during 2026 Iran tensions) — this minor discrepancy required no extra work but could cause confusion
insights.would_multipass_help: no — Round 1 queries were sufficient. The specific audio details (unit, base, targets) are so distinctive that a single targeted query surfaces multiple authoritative fact-checks and POW records immediately.
insights.deepseek_advice: For tweets claiming a current military event with video, extract any specific unit names, base locations, or operational details from the media description and search those alongside the claimed event date — old footage recycled as new news almost always has a mismatch between those specifics and any current corroborating sources. If no mainstream news corroborates a dramatic military claim, pair a direct event search with a fact-check brand suffix ('fact check' or 'leadstories snopes') to surface debunks quickly.
